methodological_rigor.justification: The study applies AI-based TIL quantification (HALO Object Phenotyper) to a reasonably large single-institution EC cohort (n=659) with long follow-up (median 63 months). Classifier training is documented (2235 lymphocytes, F1=0.81) and the ROC-derived cutoff is validated by sensitivity analyses using quartile-based alternatives. Multivariate Cox regression with backward stepwise selection identifies TIL status as an independent prognostic factor for PFS (HR 0.61) and OS (HR 0.54). Key limitations include: single-centre retrospective design with no external validation; ROC cutoff determination from the same dataset used for survival analysis introduces optimism; inter-observer reproducibility of manual invasive-frontline annotation was not assessed; POLE status not evaluated; training dataset is small (4 cases, 2235 lymphocytes).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This retrospective single-institution cohort study (Oxford LoE 4) addresses a clinically relevant question — AI-based standardisation of TIL assessment in EC. The identification of TIL status as an independent prognostic factor for PFS and OS is clinically meaningful, particularly for aggressive histological subtypes. However, without external validation and POLE status integration, the model is not ready for clinical implementation. The findings extend existing knowledge about TILs in EC into the AI-quantification domain.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK applies as a prognostic biomarker study. Cohort characteristics, inclusion/exclusion criteria, statistical methods, and key results are reported. Exploratory area-selection analyses are included in supplementary data. The ROC AUC of 0.573 (essentially chance-level) is reported honestly, and sensitivity analyses for cutoff selection are provided. However, no external validation cohort exists, POLE status is absent, F1 score is based on only two test cases, and no data or code are publicly deposited. The AI platform (HALO) is commercial and parameter details are partially described.

novelty_literature.justification: AI-based quantification of TILs in EC is a novel methodological application in this disease site; prior work in EC has relied on manual scoring. The specific approach of evaluating TILs at the invasive frontline using an automated 500 μm zone is novel in EC. The study is an incremental extension of manual TIL prognostic work (including prior publications by the same group) into AI-assisted quantification, and addresses a known methodological gap around standardisation of TIL evaluation in EC.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-structured and clearly written with explicit description of the AI training process, ROC analysis, and subgroup results. Figures are logically described. Limitations are acknowledged comprehensively in a dedicated paragraph. The discussion contextualises the F1 score appropriately against published benchmarks. The conclusion is appropriately cautious given the single-centre design. Minor weakness: the very low AUC (0.573) for the ROC model is not critically discussed as a limitation.

key_strengths: Relatively large single-institution cohort (n=659) with long follow-up (median 63 months) and comprehensive clinicopathological data
AI-based TIL quantification with documented classifier training, F1 score validation, and sensitivity analyses for cutoff selection
TIL status independently predicts both PFS and OS in multivariate analysis, including in the clinically important aggressive histological subtype
Thorough and honest limitations discussion, acknowledging the absence of POLE status, external validation, and annotation reproducibility
key_concerns: ROC cutoff (AUC 0.573, near chance level) derived from the same dataset used for survival analysis creates circular validation and inflated prognostic estimates
No external validation cohort; single-centre Japanese institution limits generalisability
AI classifier trained on only 4 cases (2235 lymphocytes), with F1 score evaluated on only 2 test cases — insufficient to demonstrate robustness
POLE mutation status not assessed, limiting integration with current 2023 FIGO molecular classification of EC
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically competent single-centre prognostic study that makes a meaningful contribution to AI-based TIL evaluation in EC, but is constrained by the absence of external validation and circular ROC-based cutoff selection. Suitable for Tier 3 after minor revisions addressing the AUC interpretation and clarifying the statistical approach.
